title: Stand up a data warehouse & BI
summary: Configure Snowflake/BigQuery with data pipelines from production systems and Metabase dashboards.

parts.title: Set up the data warehouse
parts.guidance: Use representative source data and reporting queries to choose the warehouse. Compare expected refresh delay, query behavior, access controls, operating effort and billing model, with data-location constraints explicit. Provision the selected account and initial resources within the data owner's access and budget scope. Start with a limited dataset that can reveal ingestion and modeling problems before copying production history or building executive reports on it.

options.title: Default — Set up the data warehouse
options.summary: For Snowflake, choose the account, region, database/schema and warehouse compute settings for the trial workload. Review size, suspension/resumption and query timeouts within the data owner's authorized resource scope. Test loading and reporting with separate limited identities, then inspect query behavior and measured usage. Adjust compute from the observed workload; keep warehouse compute cost visible alongside storage and other costs when comparing the trial with the proposed budget.

execution.rationale: Snowflake documents SQL/CLI account and warehouse controls, constrained users/roles, staged loading, report queries and query history. Currency-usage views cover compute, storage and transfer costs with reporting delay and reseller restrictions; authorized access and budget limits remain prerequisites.

options.title: BigQuery (GCP-standardized)
options.summary: Use the intended Google Cloud project and dataset location, with ingestion and reader permissions limited to their jobs. Check which BigQuery pricing model the company selected before choosing cost controls. For on-demand queries, inspect estimated bytes processed and set suitable limits before running an expensive trial. Test a small load and a representative report under the data owner's authorized scope. Limit ingestion to authorized data locations.
options.when: GCP-standardized stack - the warehouse is serverless BigQuery

execution.rationale: BigQuery's bq CLI supports dataset creation, small loads and bounded query trials under the approved project.

options.title: MotherDuck (small data)
options.summary: Trial MotherDuck with the data volume, queries and client connections the team expects to use. Check its current region, organization access and billing arrangement, then load a representative subset within the data owner's authorized scope. Test a report, a changed source record and an export that another tool can read. Compare measured cost and operating effort with the alternatives using the same workload.
options.when: Seed-stage data volumes - a DuckDB-based warehouse over an enterprise platform

execution.rationale: MotherDuck documents browser organization/region and billing controls alongside SQL loading, updates, reporting and export through its client. The trial therefore includes browser work, not just a connection. Use the supported client for local export; full database copying is restricted in the web UI, and usage visibility depends on permissions and plan.

parts.title: Configure CDP event sources
parts.guidance: Map each application source to its event names, identifiers and permitted properties. Keep development and production traffic distinguishable. Send synthetic records through the customer-data platform and inspect the actual payload, including timestamps, user/account identity and unexpected personal fields. Enable live collection only within the data owner's approved source and destination scope. Check how a renamed event or duplicate submission will appear before downstream models depend on those fields.

execution.rationale: Segment supports source setup and synthetic event ingestion through its HTTP interface, with raw payload inspection in the browser debugger. Separate source credentials distinguish environments; validate renamed events and message IDs. The debugger samples incoming events, so it cannot prove downstream completeness or deduplication.

parts.title: Draft the warehouse data models
parts.guidance: Define what one row represents before joining tables: an account, event, invoice or line item can produce very different totals. Map keys and fields to their sources, and specify how updates, duplicates, late arrivals, missing values and timezones are handled. Build a small sample and trace representative rows through each transformation. Label unsettled definitions for measures such as revenue or active customers and show how each proposed definition changes the result.

execution.rationale: Develop and test warehouse transformation models against supplied samples with explicit row grain and edge cases.

parts.title: Connect the CDP to the warehouse
parts.guidance: Configure the documented connector for the chosen source and warehouse using a limited ingestion identity. Check supported types, destination tables and historical-load behavior before enabling the data owner's authorized transfer scope. Start with a small load and compare source records with destination rows, keys and timestamps. For Segment warehouse connections, evaluate freshness against the documented batch-loading behavior. Establish how operators will detect a failed sync and restart it safely.

execution.rationale: Segment documents warehouse connector setup and batch-loading behavior for the approved destination.

parts.title: Verify data pipelines
parts.guidance: Reconcile a known source interval after its load should have completed. Compare counts and totals, then inspect duplicates, missing keys, updates and timezone boundaries that aggregate counts can conceal. Replay a controlled failed or delayed load and check whether recovery omits or duplicates records. Investigate discrepancies before dashboards rely on the tables, and expose the last successful refresh so report readers can recognize stale data.

execution.rationale: Failure replay and sync verification require the actual source, connector and warehouse configuration.

parts.title: Set up Metabase dashboards
parts.guidance: Connect Metabase with the authorized reporting identity and expose the models needed by its audience. Check data permissions and dashboard/collection permissions separately, then view the result as an ordinary reader. Reconcile chart totals with direct warehouse queries and test filters on known records. Share or schedule notifications only for the intended recipients, checking which fields and links they can see in the delivered report.

execution.rationale: Metabase documents dashboard building, filters and permissions for the approved reporting connection.

parts.title: Create executive dashboard
parts.guidance: Select metrics tied to the executive team's recurring decisions, with a definition, period, source and business owner for each. Show the comparison that makes a change interpretable, such as the previous period or plan. Reconcile financial numbers with the finance report before distributing the dashboard through its authorized audience. Label freshness and exclusions, and link unexpected movements to the supporting account, cohort or transaction detail.

execution.rationale: The preceding step selects Metabase. Its dashboard editor supports report queries, comparisons, explanatory text and detail links; permissions and subscriptions control distribution. Reconcile the supplied finance figures before sharing, and verify drill-through access separately because it requires query-building permissions.

metadata.supportReason: Snowflake/Segment APIs support configuration. Data modeling and dashboard design need human decisions.
